title: Flaky: PeerInstallProbeTests fallback-to-version test fails on Windows with generated batch script
job_name: Tests / No-package tests (regular, Aspire.Cli.Tests, Cli, Cli, tests/Aspire.Cli.Tests/Aspire.Cli.Tests.cs... / Cli (windows-latest)
error_pattern:
Expected PeerProbeResult.Ok, got PeerProbeResult.Failed. Reason:
Peer produced no usable output (and --version fallback). Test uses a generated FakePeerScript .cmd file on Windows that routes 'doctor' and '--version' invocations via findstr; the --version fallback branch did not produce usable output as expected.
analysis: The test exercises CLI peer-install probe fallback logic via a dynamically generated Windows batch script, invoked through cmd.exe with findstr-based argument matching. This code path and test file are unrelated to the PR's changes (Kestrel certificate configuration in Aspire.Hosting). The failure indicates the CMD interpreter or process invocation did not behave as the test expected for the --version fallback branch, consistent with an environment/timing-sensitive issue on Windows CI runners rather than a code regression from the PR.
